questions.q: What property makes SHAP explanations easy to verify for a single prediction?
options: The contributions are always positive
The contributions are always the same as permutation importance
There is one contribution per row instead of per feature
The base value plus the feature contributions add up exactly to the model's output for that row
questions.explain: SHAP is additive: for customer 0 the base value -1.072 plus the five contributions gave -1.08, matching the model's own log-odds output.

questions.q: For the gradient-boosting classifier in the lesson, in what units were the SHAP values expressed?
options: Log-odds, so the total can be converted to a probability
Percentage points of churn probability
Standard deviations of each feature
Dollars of revenue
questions.explain: TreeExplainer on this scikit-learn boosted classifier explains the raw log-odds output. Convert to probability (about 0.254 for customer 0) when presenting.

questions.q: In the summary (beeswarm) plot, red high-tenure dots sit on the left of zero. What does that mean?
options: Long tenure pushes the predicted churn risk down
Long tenure pushes the predicted churn risk up
Tenure is not used by the model
Those customers were removed from the test set
questions.explain: Left of zero means a negative SHAP value, lowering predicted churn. Red means the feature value is high, so high tenure reduces predicted risk.

questions.q: Mean absolute SHAP values give which kind of explanation?
options: A local explanation for one customer only
A causal effect of each feature
A global ranking of how much each feature moves predictions on average
A fairness audit
questions.explain: Averaging the absolute SHAP values across rows summarizes each feature's typical influence globally, without showing direction.

questions.q: Which caution is most appropriate when presenting SHAP results?
options: SHAP proves that changing a feature will change the real-world outcome
SHAP explains what the fitted model does, not necessarily how the real world works, and correlated features can share credit
SHAP results never depend on the model chosen
SHAP should never be shown to non-technical audiences
questions.explain: SHAP describes model behavior. It does not establish causation, and correlated features can split credit in ways that need careful interpretation.
